settings_schema_impacts.note: Nine value states are demonstrated (default, recommended, inherited, auto, not-configured, managed, custom, unavailable, effective-differs); the schema needs a valueSource enum plus managedReason/unavailableReason strings, not a boolean.

standard | advanced | expert | managed | diagnostic | unavailable are all rendered distinctly (expert requires deliberate unlock; diagnostic lives in a per-domain drawer). A simple|advanced two-tier model cannot express this.

Roles, models, goal route classes, BSD route, crew concurrency, and permission rules all need paired requested/effective values with a human 'why'; the schema should make this a first-class shape rather than per-feature ad hoc fields.

Ordered rule collections (permissions), keyed template collections (crew), and structured route classes (goal) do not fit scalar rows; the registry needs collection-valued settings with their own event grammar.

schema_event_storage_impacts.note: The trace (input, matched rule numbers, winner, explanation) is a queryable event product; rule reorders must re-emit it. Storage owner should keep traces with run evidence for audit.

Update attempts are two-entry honest histories (verification-failed then rolled-back) with per-condition verification results; exit code alone is never success and must not be an event terminal state.
Gist edits must store the previous wording in the version entry for restore to be real; this concept demonstrates restore failing honestly when older versions lack stored text.
Per-request admitted/omitted blocks with token counts are receipts, implying an event stream from the prompt assembler that Settings only projects.

slint_port_impacts.note: Two-column grid rows (content | marginalia) map to a Slint HorizontalLayout with a fixed-preferred-width side column; the hairline is an inset shadow in web, a 1px Rectangle in Slint.
CSS dotted-border leaders map to a custom drawn dotted line element; the sliding ink marker maps to an animated y-property on a small Rectangle, teleporting under reduced motion.
Move up/down buttons (no drag) were chosen deliberately so the statute book ports to Slint as a plain model reorder without drag-and-drop infrastructure.
The trace is a pure data projection (rows with matched/winner flags); no DOM measurement is involved, so it ports as a ListView over a computed model.
position:sticky maps to a fixed header row above a Flickable, as noted inline in the CSS.
Appendix bodies render on entry open (aria-expanded state), never eagerly; in Slint this is conditional component instantiation per expanded row.

unresolved_questions: Should a user-authored rule be able to out-rank a workspace-managed deny by position, or do managed rules always pin to the tail of the book? This concept pins managed rows in place and blocks displacement; canon must decide the general rule.
Per-Persona profiles: is the narrower-only constraint enforced by construction (profiles are subsets) or by evaluation-time flooring? The UI asserts narrower-only; the mechanism is unspecified.
Goal fan-out: is the configured ceiling per Goal, per project, or global? Rendered here as global+project scope; the runtime owner must fix the scope chain.
Does the BSD latency budget stack with provider timeout budgets or subsume them?
Settings census: 817 vs 825 vs 826 rows across artifacts — which figure is canon before new rows are minted?
